<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

PR #41364 adds `topk_page_transform`, which combines DeepSelect Top-K selection with the page-table transform in its epilogue.

DeepSeek V4.1 on Hopper still uses:

```text
torch.topk
  -> sort raw indices
  -> gather physical KV slots
```

This PR connects the new DeepSelect operator to that runtime path.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

- Use `topk_page_transform` for the SM90 full-topk decode path.
- Write transformed int32 KV slots directly into the existing output buffer.
- Preserve raw-index ordering with `sorted_index=True`.
- Keep the existing Torch path when raw indices are also required.
- Keep SM100 and newer architectures on the existing DeepGEMM path.
- Add CPU dispatch/fallback tests and an H20 runtime integration test.

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on NVIDIA H20:

| Test | Result |
|---|---:|
| DeepSelect kernel tests | 10/10 passed |
| Related indexer unit tests | 28/28 passed |
| New runtime integration tests | 5/5 passed |
| `_torch_decode` statement coverage | 90% |

Coverage includes short contexts where `width < topk`, variable row lengths, page-table mapping, sorted output, and the raw-index fallback.


<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling


The replaced region was benchmarked on NVIDIA H20 with CUDA 13.0 and PyTorch 2.13. Each complete run used 20 warmup iterations followed by 5 groups of 100 measurements. The table reports the mean of the medians from two complete runs.

The measured regions were:

```text
Before:
torch.topk -> raw-index sort -> slot gather -> output copy

After:
DeepSelect top-k -> sorted-index epilogue -> page-table transform
```

| Rows | Width | Top-K | Before | After | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 32K | 512 | 163.264 us | 31.744 us | 5.14x |
| 8 | 32K | 512 | 163.992 us | 31.592 us | 5.19x |
| 32 | 32K | 512 | 163.664 us | 31.456 us | 5.20x |
| 1 | 128K | 1024 | 162.864 us | 31.760 us | 5.13x |
| 8 | 128K | 1024 | 164.960 us | 32.480 us | 5.08x |

This is a microbenchmark of the replaced Top-K and transform region, not an end-to-end serving throughput claim.

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

nodes.body: `sorted_index=True` preserves the existing decode behavior. The previous `write_decode()` path explicitly call `sidx.sort(dim=-1)` , and `Selection.page_indices` is documented as ascending. This sorts logical indices, not values, before the page-table transform. The sort is fused into the DeepSelect kernel rather than adding another PyTorch kernel launch.

nodes.body: Setting `sorted_index=False` does not change the Top-K set, and FlashMLA does not require indices to be ordered. However, it would alter the existing output-ordering contract and change the floating-point accumulation order inside FlashMLA, so the attention outputs would no longer be bitwise identical. With the default `index_topk=512`, removing the sort saves at most about `0.29 us` inside the DeepSelect kernel; when the subsequent FlashMLA dual-cache decode is included in the measurement, no stable benefit is observed. The gain does not justify the contract change and the loss of determinism, so `full_topk.py` should be left unchanged.

@@ -138,6 +145,20 @@ def _torch_decode(self, inputs: DecodeInputs, out: Selection) -> None:
         )
         if d is None:
             return
+        # Sparse prefill consumers need raw positions as well as mapped slots;
+        # the fused DeepSelect epilogue intentionally returns mapped slots only.
+        if self.use_deep_select_decode and out.raw_indices is None:
+            metadata = inputs.paged_metadata
+            topk_page_transform(
+                d.scores,

+                end=d.lens.to(torch.int32),
+                sorted_index=True,

inline_comments.body: `sorted_index=True` preserves the existing decode behavior. The previous `write_decode()` path explicitly call `sidx.sort(dim=-1)` , and `Selection.page_indices` is documented as ascending. This sorts logical indices, not values, before the page-table transform. The sort is fused into the DeepSelect kernel rather than adding another PyTorch kernel launch.

inline_comments.body: Setting `sorted_index=False` does not change the Top-K set, and FlashMLA does not require indices to be ordered. However, it would alter the existing output-ordering contract and change the floating-point accumulation order inside FlashMLA, so the attention outputs would no longer be bitwise identical. With the default `index_topk=512`, removing the sort saves at most about `0.29 us` inside the DeepSelect kernel; when the subsequent FlashMLA dual-cache decode is included in the measurement, no stable benefit is observed. The gain does not justify the contract change and the loss of determinism, so `full_topk.py` should be left unchanged.
